claims.claim_text_verbatim: Based on this formulation, we introduce MedBenchAgent, a multi-agent framework with a Benchmark Intermediate Representation (BIR) that encodes task definitions, evidence mappings, evaluation protocols, and item specifications across construction stages.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent introduces a multi-agent framework with a unified BIR structure

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent separates planning, which derives and verifies the specification, from instantiation, which constructs and audits items under the locked specification.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent separates planning specifications from concrete item instantiation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, outperforming direct task induction (79.2–80.0%) and prior-guided induction (85.1%); 994 of 1,000 sampled items from correctly identified tasks pass human audit.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent reaches 90.9% Task-Space F1 and 99.4% human audit pass rate

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We further demonstrate portability to a specialized medical domain and evaluate twelve VLMs, revealing task- and setting-specific variation obscured by aggregate scores.
claims.claim_summary: Demonstrates domain portability and uncovers fine-grained VLM performance variations

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results establish constrained compilation as a scalable and auditable framework for medical VLM benchmark construction beyond question generation.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained compilation provides a scalable and auditable framework for benchmark creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We address this challenge with MedBenchAgent, a multi-agent framework for systematic medical VLM benchmark construction.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent provides a multi-agent system for systematic medical VLM benchmark creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: We cast benchmark construction as constrained compilation, in which the benchmark specification is progressively established from an intended evaluation scope, heterogeneous source annotations, and medical knowledge, with each confirmed decision narrowing the space of subsequent construction.
claims.claim_summary: Formulates benchmark construction as constrained compilation across stages

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together, constrained compilation and the BIR provide an explicit mechanism for carrying semantic and evidential constraints from benchmark specification into downstream construction.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained compilation and BIR explicitly preserve semantic and evidential constraints

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In this way, MedBenchAgent extends automation from predefined medical scopes or question structures to benchmark specification itself, while preserving the annotation and medical constraints required for reliable construction.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent automates benchmark specification while preserving medical and annotation constraints

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In construction analysis, MedBenchAgent achieves a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct task induction and 85.1% when the same task prior is provided to the direct model.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent beats direct and prior-guided task induction in F1 score

claims.claim_text_verbatim: For correctly identified tasks, 994 of 1,000 sampled items pass human audit.
claims.claim_summary: 994 out of 1,000 generated items pass human audit review

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Model evaluation reveals substantial variation across tasks, imaging settings, and evaluation metrics that aggregate scores can obscure, reinforcing fine-grained benchmark specification as an important component of medical VLM evaluation.
claims.claim_summary: Evaluation reveals task and metric variations masked by overall aggregate scores

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Table 1, BIR-mediated construction achieves 90.9% Task-Space F1, compared with 79.2–80.0% for direct induction.
claims.claim_summary: BIR-mediated task planning achieves 90.9% Task-Space F1

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Providing T0 improves direct DeepSeek-V4-Flash induction to 85.1% F1, while MedBenchAgent further increases precision from 76.9% to 87.0% at the same 95.2% recall, reducing false positives from six to three.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent raises precision to 87.0% and reduces false positive tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All methods achieve 100% EMA on matched tasks.
claims.claim_summary: All tested methods achieve 100% evidence-mapping agreement on matched tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Table 2 shows that 994 items pass, yielding a 99.4% consistency rate.
claims.claim_summary: Human audit confirms a 99.4% item consistency rate

claims.claim_text_verbatim: As shown in Table 3, medical VLMs outperform general-purpose VLMs by 6.23 points in Overall Acc. but trail by 2.48 points on AC, indicating that the aggregate advantage is not uniform across tasks.
claims.claim_summary: Medical VLMs beat general models overall but trail on assessment tasks

claims.claim_text_verbatim: To quantify such changes, we compare all 66 model pairs and find that 12–24 pairs (18.2–36.4%) reverse ordering between Overall Acc. and individual-task Acc.; within tasks, 4–15 pairs (6.1–22.7%) reverse between Acc. and F1.
claims.claim_summary: Model relative rankings reverse frequently across tasks and evaluation metrics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across these measures, 28–34 of 66 model pairs (42.4–51.5%) reverse ordering relative to Overall Acc.
claims.claim_summary: Over 40% of model rank pairs flip between overall accuracy and spatial metrics

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across four medical VLMs, Acc. decreases by 5.86–17.97 percentage points (pp) and F1 by 6.33–22.61 pp (Table 5).
claims.claim_summary: Image blurring causes consistent drop in accuracy and F1 across medical VLMs

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All seven proposed tasks and their supporting-field mappings were retained without task-space revision.
claims.claim_summary: All seven ISIC dermoscopy task plans passed task-space review without changes

claims.claim_text_verbatim: All sampled items passed checks of reference–evidence consistency, task–query consistency, and evaluation-format integrity against the normalized annotations and locked task contracts.
claims.claim_summary: 100% of sampled cross-domain items passed all consistency and integrity audits

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Our analyses identify open-ended task-space specification as the primary source of construction uncertainty, while annotation-evidence mapping and item instantiation become substantially more reliable once benchmark semantics are fixed.
claims.claim_summary: Fixing benchmark semantics stabilizes downstream mapping and item creation

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Together with the cross-domain instantiation under a specialized medical setting, these results show that constrained, multi-agent benchmark construction can support both scalable medical VLM evaluation and systematic study of the benchmark-construction process itself.
claims.claim_summary: Constrained multi-agent framework enables scalable evaluation and benchmark meta-analysis

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent operationalizes this formulation through a staged multi-agent workflow for medical benchmark construction: 1) planning resolves and verifies the specification against dataset annotations and medical references before locking the BIR; and 2) instantiation constructs and audits evaluation items under this fixed specification.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent operationalizes this formulation through a staged multi-agent workflow for medical benchmark construction: 1) planning resolves and verifies the specification against dataset annotations and medical references before locking the BIR; and 2) instantiation constructs and audits evaluation items under this fixed specification.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This formulation enables empirical evaluation of both the benchmark-construction process and the benchmark produced by MedBenchAgent.
claims.claim_summary: This formulation enables empirical evaluation of both the benchmark-construction process and the benchmark produced by MedBenchAgent.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Overall, this work makes three contributions: (1) Conceptually, we model the construction of medical VLM benchmarks and formulate it as constrained compilation; (2) Methodologically, we introduce a multi-agent MedBenchAgent framework and its Benchmark Intermediate Representation (BIR); and (3) Empirically, we derive insights into both the benchmark-construction process and medical VLM evaluation, while providing reusable benchmark artifacts.
claims.claim_summary: Overall, this work makes three contributions: (1) Conceptually, we model the construction of medical VLM benchmarks and formulate it as constrained compilation; (2) Methodologically, we introduce a multi-agent MedBenchAgent framework and its Benchmark Intermediate Representation (BIR); and (3) Empirically, we derive insights into both the benchmark-construction process and medical VLM evaluation, while providing reusable benchmark artifacts.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This separates benchmark construction, which defines the evaluation object, from benchmark application, which produces evidence about model behavior under the specified scope and protocol.
claims.claim_summary: This separates benchmark construction, which defines the evaluation object, from benchmark application, which produces evidence about model behavior under the specified scope and protocol.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The formulation above motivates three desiderata for medical VLM benchmark construction.
claims.claim_summary: The formulation above motivates three desiderata for medical VLM benchmark construction.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This step connects an evidence-supported task to its medical evaluation semantics, thereby supporting Desideratum D2.
claims.claim_summary: This step connects an evidence-supported task to its medical evaluation semantics, thereby supporting Desideratum D2.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This separation allows linguistic variation in the query while preserving annotation-grounded reference answers and the item-level entailment requirement of Desideratum D1.
claims.claim_summary: This separation allows linguistic variation in the query while preserving annotation-grounded reference answers and the item-level entailment requirement of Desideratum D1.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent uses BIR-mediated task planning to constrain task-space construction with U and Σm, rather than inducing the task space in a single open-ended step.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent uses BIR-mediated task planning to constrain task-space construction with U and Σm, rather than inducing the task space in a single open-ended step.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The high consistency rate supports locked specifications for large-scale item construction while identifying targets for semantic verification.
claims.claim_summary: The high consistency rate supports locked specifications for large-scale item construction while identifying targets for semantic verification.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent promotes consistent item construction by locking item-construction requirements in the confirmed specification before instantiation.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent promotes consistent item construction by locking item-construction requirements in the confirmed specification before instantiation.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent retains annotation-supported prediction targets as separate tasks and records their evaluation protocols in the BIR.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent retains annotation-supported prediction targets as separate tasks and records their evaluation protocols in the BIR.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent treats the annotations associated with each source image as the reference standard.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent treats the annotations associated with each source image as the reference standard.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The consistent degradation indicates that benchmark performance remains sensitive to visual evidence from the corresponding image, despite references being derived directly from source annotations rather than model-based visual judgments.
claims.claim_summary: The consistent degradation indicates that benchmark performance remains sensitive to visual evidence from the corresponding image, despite references being derived directly from source annotations rather than model-based visual judgments.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results provide cross-domain evidence for the portability of MedBenchAgent across annotation semantics and task definitions.
claims.claim_summary: These results provide cross-domain evidence for the portability of MedBenchAgent across annotation semantics and task definitions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These phases provide a clinically structured progression from basic image interpretation to increasingly integrated diagnostic decisions, while remaining expressed as model-evaluable visual prediction capabilities.
claims.claim_summary: These phases provide a clinically structured progression from basic image interpretation to increasingly integrated diagnostic decisions, while remaining expressed as model-evaluable visual prediction capabilities.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: MedBenchAgent’s residual errors are concentrated in semantic boundary cases, including a redundant BUS-BRA finding-type proposal, a visual-grounding proposal that did not define a capability distinct from generic detection, a shortcut-prone VinDr view-identification task, and the omitted finding-level assessment target.
claims.claim_summary: MedBenchAgent’s residual errors are concentrated in semantic boundary cases, including a redundant BUS-BRA finding-type proposal, a visual-grounding proposal that did not define a capability distinct from generic detection, a shortcut-prone VinDr view-identification task, and the omitted finding-level assessment target.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, the direct baselines more frequently introduce nonvisual metadata, acquisition or marker shortcuts, invalid spatial evidence, or omit otherwise supported visual prediction targets.
claims.claim_summary: In contrast, the direct baselines more frequently introduce nonvisual metadata, acquisition or marker shortcuts, invalid spatial evidence, or omit otherwise supported visual prediction targets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Importantly, the fixed annotation-derived reference answers remained supported by the authorized evidence in all six cases.
claims.claim_summary: Importantly, the fixed annotation-derived reference answers remained supported by the authorized evidence in all six cases.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Across the complete audit, there were four task–query-alignment failures and six evaluation-integrity failures, with no reference-groundedness or unambiguity failures.
claims.claim_summary: Across the complete audit, there were four task–query-alignment failures and six evaluation-integrity failures, with no reference-groundedness or unambiguity failures.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Different checkpoints lead on different task metrics, providing complementary evaluation profiles.
claims.claim_summary: Different checkpoints lead on different task metrics, providing complementary evaluation profiles.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In particular, categorical performance does not reliably predict spatial-localization performance.
claims.claim_summary: In particular, categorical performance does not reliably predict spatial-localization performance.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: BreastGPT-8B achieves the highest aggregate finding-attribute scores, yet its BrEaST Macro- F1 ranges from 78.0 on margin and 63.7 on halo to 33.2 on posterior features and 35.0 on calcifications (Table 12).
claims.claim_summary: BreastGPT-8B achieves the highest aggregate finding-attribute scores, yet its BrEaST Macro- F1 ranges from 78.0 on margin and 63.7 on halo to 33.2 on posterior features and 35.0 on calcifications (Table 12).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On posterior features, QoQ-Med-7B achieves higher Accuracy than BreastGPT-8B (57.9 versus 54.8), whereas BreastGPT- 8B achieves higher Macro-F1 (33.2 versus 25.8).
claims.claim_summary: On posterior features, QoQ-Med-7B achieves higher Accuracy than BreastGPT-8B (57.9 versus 54.8), whereas BreastGPT- 8B achieves higher Macro-F1 (33.2 versus 25.8).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The same ordering reversal occurs on halo: QoQ-Med-7B leads in Accuracy (72.0 versus 70.3), but BreastGPT-8B leads in Macro-F1 (63.7 versus 41.8).
claims.claim_summary: The same ordering reversal occurs on halo: QoQ-Med-7B leads in Accuracy (72.0 versus 70.3), but BreastGPT-8B leads in Macro-F1 (63.7 versus 41.8).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These reversals extend the metric-dependent rankings observed in the main results to atomic prediction targets.
claims.claim_summary: These reversals extend the metric-dependent rankings observed in the main results to atomic prediction targets.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Accuracy weights individual items equally, while Macro-F1 averages class-specific F1 scores; consequently, the two metrics capture different aspects of performance over the answer space.
claims.claim_summary: Accuracy weights individual items equally, while Macro-F1 averages class-specific F1 scores; consequently, the two metrics capture different aspects of performance over the answer space.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Qwen3-VL-8B-T exceeds Qwen3-VL-8B-I by only 0.60 Accuracy points overall, but the task-level changes are much larger (Table 3).
claims.claim_summary: Qwen3-VL-8B-T exceeds Qwen3-VL-8B-I by only 0.60 Accuracy points overall, but the task-level changes are much larger (Table 3).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: FA improves by 27.09 points, while AA, FT, AC, DX, and PS decrease by 9.37, 1.22, 0.53, 4.85, and 7.50 points, respectively.
claims.claim_summary: FA improves by 27.09 points, while AA, FT, AC, DX, and PS decrease by 9.37, 1.22, 0.53, 4.85, and 7.50 points, respectively.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Under the reported equal weighting of task families, the FA improvement contributes approximately 4.52 points to Overall Accuracy, while the other five tasks jointly contribute approximately −3.91 points.
claims.claim_summary: Under the reported equal weighting of task families, the FA improvement contributes approximately 4.52 points to Overall Accuracy, while the other five tasks jointly contribute approximately −3.91 points.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The small net change thus results from opposing task-level changes rather than uniformly similar performance.
claims.claim_summary: The small net change thus results from opposing task-level changes rather than uniformly similar performance.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: The FA improvement is itself concentrated in particular attributes.
claims.claim_summary: The FA improvement is itself concentrated in particular attributes.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On BrEaST, halo Accuracy increases from 11.4 to 63.4 and skin-thickening Accuracy from 2.7 to 76.6, whereas posterior-feature Accuracy decreases from 37.3 to 22.2 (Table 12).
claims.claim_summary: On BrEaST, halo Accuracy increases from 11.4 to 63.4 and skin-thickening Accuracy from 2.7 to 76.6, whereas posterior-feature Accuracy decreases from 37.3 to 22.2 (Table 12).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: With seven equally weighted attributes, the halo and skin-thickening increases together contribute approximately 18.0 points to the roughly 27.1-point FA improvement, based on the rounded attribute scores.
claims.claim_summary: With seven equally weighted attributes, the halo and skin-thickening increases together contribute approximately 18.0 points to the roughly 27.1-point FA improvement, based on the rounded attribute scores.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Decomposing the comparison at both levels therefore reveals a pattern that the Overall score obscures: a substantial gain within one task family is driven largely by a subset of its prediction targets and offset by declines elsewhere.
claims.claim_summary: Decomposing the comparison at both levels therefore reveals a pattern that the Overall score obscures: a substantial gain within one task family is driven largely by a subset of its prediction targets and offset by declines elsewhere.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Within Lingshu, the 32B checkpoint improves Overall Accuracy from 47.00 to 50.73 and FA Macro-F1 from 38.66 to 43.01 relative to the 7B checkpoint, while DX Macro-F1 decreases from 29.29 to 24.54.
claims.claim_summary: Within Lingshu, the 32B checkpoint improves Overall Accuracy from 47.00 to 50.73 and FA Macro-F1 from 38.66 to 43.01 relative to the 7B checkpoint, while DX Macro-F1 decreases from 29.29 to 24.54.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: In contrast, Qwen3-VL-32B improves over Qwen3-VL-8B-I on aggregate multiple-choice performance and all three reported breast-imaging spatial settings (Tables 3 and 4).
claims.claim_summary: In contrast, Qwen3-VL-32B improves over Qwen3-VL-8B-I on aggregate multiple-choice performance and all three reported breast-imaging spatial settings (Tables 3 and 4).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These checkpoint comparisons show that aggregate improvements can have different task-level compositions.
claims.claim_summary: These checkpoint comparisons show that aggregate improvements can have different task-level compositions.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: They support examining the resulting performance profile rather than using model scale or the thinking designation as a substitute for task-specific evaluation.
claims.claim_summary: They support examining the resulting performance profile rather than using model scale or the thinking designation as a substitute for task-specific evaluation.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: On ISIC, Hulu-Med-7B achieves the highest diagnosis Accuracy and Macro-F1 among the evaluated checkpoints (56.3 and 34.4), but obtains 0.7 mIoU and 0.2 Acc@IoU0.5 on detection.
claims.claim_summary: On ISIC, Hulu-Med-7B achieves the highest diagnosis Accuracy and Macro-F1 among the evaluated checkpoints (56.3 and 34.4), but obtains 0.7 mIoU and 0.2 Acc@IoU0.5 on detection.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Qwen3-VL-8B-I achieves lower diagnosis scores (53.2 and 22.8), yet substantially higher detection scores (80.3 and 91.4; Table 10).
claims.claim_summary: Qwen3-VL-8B-I achieves lower diagnosis scores (53.2 and 22.8), yet substantially higher detection scores (80.3 and 91.4; Table 10).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: These results describe complementary task profiles within the same dataset family.
claims.claim_summary: These results describe complementary task profiles within the same dataset family.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: Spatial rankings also change across imaging settings.
claims.claim_summary: Spatial rankings also change across imaging settings.

claims.claim_text_verbatim: BreastGPT-8B leads Qwen3-VL-32B on BUS-BRA detection, with Acc@IoU0.5 of 82.80 versus 62.08, whereas Qwen3-VL-32B leads on VinDr-Mammo detection, with 12.86 versus 0.90 (Table 4).
claims.claim_summary: BreastGPT-8B leads Qwen3-VL-32B on BUS-BRA detection, with Acc@IoU0.5 of 82.80 versus 62.08, whereas Qwen3-VL-32B leads on VinDr-Mammo detection, with 12.86 versus 0.90 (Table 4).

claims.claim_text_verbatim: This ranking reversal shows that a model’s advantage within one localization setting need not persist in another.
claims.claim_summary: This ranking reversal shows that a model’s advantage within one localization setting need not persist in another.
